# D.scribe

> D.scribe is voice-to-manuscript software that turns the talks, sermons, and coaching sessions you have already recorded into a finished book, for speakers, pastors, and coaches.

D.scribe (also written D.Scribe) is web software. You upload recordings you already have, such as sermons, keynotes, coaching calls, podcast episodes or voice memos (MP3, MP4, WAV, M4A, or a YouTube link), or you talk with T.H.E.O, the built-in AI interviewer. D.scribe transcribes the audio, builds a voice profile from how you speak, plans the book's structure, drafts the manuscript chapter by chapter, and runs a coherence pass across the whole book. Every sentence lands in a built-in manuscript editor, and the finished book exports to PDF or DOCX.

D.scribe was founded in 2025 by Kyle Ingram and is based in Dallas-Fort Worth.

## Who it is for

- Speakers and keynote presenters with a backlog of recorded talks
- Pastors turning sermons and sermon series into books
- Podcasters whose best episodes deserve a second life in print
- Coaches and consultants with training content worth publishing
- Course creators turning curriculum into a companion book
- Memoirists and family historians who tell stories better out loud

## Pricing (USD)

- Free trial: 10 Ink to start. No payment required.
- Starter: $25/month, 300 Ink (about 1.5 books).
- Pro: $50/month, 660 Ink (~3 books), plus about 30 minutes a month of spoken brainstorming with T.H.E.O.
- Premium: $100/month, 1,500 Ink (~7 books), plus about 80 minutes a month of spoken brainstorming.
- Every plan includes the full toolkit: AI transcription, voice profile, chapter generation, AI coherence pass, enrichment quotes, priority generation, PDF / DOCX export. Plans differ only on capacity.
- One-time Ink and voice refills start at $20 and never expire.
- Month to month, cancel anytime. Ink is D.scribe's credit system: every AI action costs Ink, and the cost is shown before it runs.

Full details: https://www.d-scribe.app/pricing

- [Home](https://www.d-scribe.app/): What D.scribe does, how it works, and the FAQ.

- [Compare D.scribe](https://www.d-scribe.app/vs): Side-by-side comparisons with other book tools and services.
  - [D.scribe vs Built&Written](https://www.d-scribe.app/vs/builtwritten): Both turn what you already have into a book. The real difference is what you feed in: they read your writing, we listen to you talk.
  - [D.scribe vs Squibler](https://www.d-scribe.app/vs/squibler): Squibler helps you invent a story. D.scribe helps you keep the one you already told.
  - [D.scribe vs Dictate](https://www.d-scribe.app/vs/dictate): Dictate sells you a service. D.scribe sells you the tool. One costs about 200 times more and takes far longer, and for some people that is exactly the right trade.

## What makes D.scribe different

### Built for spoken content, not typing

Fiction tools like Sudowrite and NovelCrafter start from a blank page and a prompt. D.scribe starts from the recordings you already have — a sermon, a keynote, a coaching call. Sudowrite handles paragraphs. D.scribe handles books.

### One pipeline from audio to export

ChatGPT and Claude can draft passages, but they keep no project memory and export no manuscript. D.scribe carries your book from upload through transcription, structure, drafting, editing, and a finished PDF or DOCX in one place.

### Book-length output, in your voice

Repurposing tools like Castmagic and Descript cut your audio into clips and show notes. D.scribe builds a voice profile from how you actually talk and writes a full, coherent manuscript — the whole book, not the highlights.

### A ghostwriter alternative at a fraction of the cost

A professional ghostwriter typically costs $18,000 to $50,000 for a nonfiction book, according to Reedsy's pricing guide. D.scribe starts at $25 per month. Same outcome: a finished manuscript in your voice.

Source: Reedsy, "How Much Does It Cost to Hire a Ghostwriter?", https://reedsy.com/blog/guide/ghostwriter/cost-to-hire/

### Pay for what you use

Credits (called Ink) are shown before every AI action, unused credits roll over, and overage is blocked with a warning — never a surprise charge. A typical full 40,000-word book runs about 100 to 200 Ink.

D.scribe drafts; you decide. Every sentence lands in a built-in editor where you can rewrite, tighten, or add. Nothing is finished until you say it is.

## Frequently asked questions

### How does D.scribe work?

Enter the brainstorm studio to spend as much time as you like being interviewed by T.H.E.O, our specialist AI interviewer. Or, upload any existing audio — a sermon, a coaching call, a YouTube link, a podcast episode, or a voice memo. D.scribe transcribes it word-for-word, builds a structure based on your chapter targets, analyzes your themes and voice patterns, then generates a full manuscript chapter by chapter. The entire process takes minutes, not months.

### What audio formats does D.scribe support?

D.scribe accepts MP3, MP4, WAV, M4A, and most common audio and video formats. You can also paste a YouTube link and D.scribe will pull the audio automatically.

### Will the manuscript sound like me or like an AI?

Like you. Before a single chapter is written, D.scribe builds a voice profile from your recordings: your vocabulary, your sentence rhythm, the way you land a point from the pulpit or the stage. Every key point in the draft comes from your own words. Nothing invented. Nothing hallucinated. If a line drifts from how you would say it, rewrite it in the editor and the book stays yours.

### How does it maintain consistency across a multi-chapter, 40,000+ word book?

D.scribe was meticulously built to analyze audio content that maps your themes, organizes your key points and plans the ideal structure of your book BEFORE text generation starts. After the draft, an AI coherence pass reads the manuscript end to end and smooths out repeated points, shifting terminology, or gaps between chapters. So chapter nine connects appropriately to chapter two and vice versa. It is built to handle a single conversation, years' worth of sermons, and everything in between.

### How much typing will I need to do?

Less than starting from a blank page, but never none. The first draft arrives as a complete manuscript in the built-in editor, where every sentence is editable. Either insert your own text or use the 'Magic Edit' tool to tighten a story, cut a point, or add what's been left out. Nothing is finished until you say it is.

### How does Ink work?

Ink is D.scribe's credit system. Every action that uses AI (brainstorming, transcription, analysis, chapter generation and so on) costs a small amount of Ink. Starter plans include 300 Ink per month, Pro includes 660, and Premium includes 1,500. A typical full manuscript runs around 100–200 Ink depending on length. You can always see your balance before taking any action.

### How long does it take to generate a manuscript?

Most users go from upload to a full first draft in under an hour. Transcription takes a few minutes; chapter generation typically runs 2–5 minutes per chapter depending on length.

### Who is D.scribe for?

D.scribe is built for people who already have something to say — coaches, pastors, speakers, consultants, and experts who think best out loud. If you've been told you should write a book but never had the time or the process to do it, D.scribe is the bridge between your voice and a finished manuscript.

## Comparisons

Competitor details were read from their own public pages on 10 September 2026 and reflect what they advertised then. Prices and features change. Check their site before you buy.

### D.scribe vs Built&Written

Page: https://www.d-scribe.app/vs/builtwritten

Both turn what you already have into a book. The real difference is what you feed in: they read your writing, we listen to you talk.

Built&Written is the closest product to D.scribe on the market. Same buyer (coaches, founders, consultants), same promise (your material becomes a finished book), same shape (self-serve subscription software). If you are comparing us to anyone, it is them.

- What you put in: D.scribe: Raw audio: sermons, coaching calls, keynotes, voice memos, podcast episodes. Built&Written: Text you already wrote: notes, LinkedIn posts, podcast transcripts.
- Entry price: D.scribe: $25/month (Starter). Built&Written: $15/month billed annually ($180/yr), or $19/month monthly.
- Is the cheapest tier full software?: D.scribe: Yes. Every plan includes AI transcription, voice profile, chapter generation, coherence pass, and PDF/DOCX export. Tiers differ only on capacity. Built&Written: No. The Author tier is editor-only and does not include AI book writing. AI generation starts on the Entrepreneur tier at $49/month.
- Spoken ideation: D.scribe: Built in on Pro and above: a spoken brainstorming session where the AI interviews you out loud and you answer by voice. Built&Written: Not offered.
- Free trial: D.scribe: 10 Ink free to start. Built&Written: No free tier visible. A 7-day money-back guarantee instead.
- Where the book ends up: D.scribe: PDF and DOCX you own and can edit. Built&Written: Print-ready Amazon KDP output, which is their headline strength.
- Independent reviews: D.scribe: Early. This is our weakest area and we are not going to dress it up. Built&Written: Trustpilot and G2 at 4.7 of 5 from 9 reviews, plus 13 or more named testimonials with titles and tenure.

Where Built&Written is stronger: Proof and print-readiness. Built&Written has real third-party reviews and named testimonials with photos, and their KDP export is genuinely further along than ours. If proof from strangers is what unlocks your purchase, that gap matters.

Pick Built&Written if: You already write a lot and want to assemble existing text into a KDP-ready book, and you want a review history from other buyers before you commit.

Pick D.scribe if: You think out loud rather than write, and the raw material is sitting in recordings you never transcribed. D.scribe is built for the person who has 47 coaching calls and no manuscript.

- Q: Is D.scribe cheaper than Built&Written? A: $25/month monthly versus their $19/month monthly on the entry tier. Their annual rate of $15/month is lower, but that tier is editor-only. Comparable AI book generation on their side starts at $49/month.
- Q: Can I use my existing notes and posts with D.scribe? A: Yes, but audio is the native input. Text works better on Built&Written, which is designed around material you have already written.
- Q: Does D.scribe export to Amazon KDP? A: D.scribe exports PDF and DOCX, which you can format for KDP. Built&Written produces print-ready KDP output directly, and that is a real advantage for them.

### D.scribe vs Squibler

Page: https://www.d-scribe.app/vs/squibler

Squibler helps you invent a story. D.scribe helps you keep the one you already told.

Squibler is the largest player in the category by user count, with more than 20,000 writers. It is built around chatting with an AI to write fiction and screenplays. That is a different job from turning a speaker's recordings into a nonfiction manuscript.

- Built for: D.scribe: Nonfiction: coaches, pastors, speakers, consultants who already have the material in their voice. Squibler: Fiction, novels, and screenplays, plus some nonfiction.
- How the draft happens: D.scribe: You upload recordings. D.scribe transcribes, builds a voice profile, and drafts chapter by chapter. Squibler: You chat with the AI and direct the story as you go.
- Entry price: D.scribe: $25/month (Starter), 300 Ink. Squibler: Free tier with 1,000 credits/month. Plus is $15.83/month billed annually, normally $29.99/month, with 10,000 credits. Pro is $49.17/month annually, normally $89.99/month, unlimited credits.
- Free option: D.scribe: 10 Ink to start. Squibler: Yes, a real ongoing free tier. This is a genuine advantage for them.
- Voice authenticity: D.scribe: Transcripts are taken from your own audio, and a voice profile is built from them. Squibler: The AI writes in a style you steer through the chat and their style tools.
- Spoken ideation: D.scribe: Spoken brainstorming on Pro and above, where the AI interviews you out loud. Squibler: Not offered.
- Track record: D.scribe: Early. Not going to pretend otherwise. Squibler: More than 20,000 writers and named testimonials with photos.

Where Squibler is stronger: Scale, price of entry, and a free tier that is actually usable. If you want to test AI book writing at zero cost, Squibler lets you do that today and we do not. They also support far more genres.

Pick Squibler if: You are writing fiction, a novel, or a screenplay, or you want to experiment for free before spending anything.

Pick D.scribe if: You are writing nonfiction, the source material already exists as audio, and you need the finished manuscript to sound like you rather than like a chatbot you directed.

- Q: Does D.scribe have a free plan like Squibler? A: No. D.scribe gives you 10 Ink to start. Squibler has a standing free tier with 1,000 credits a month, which is a better deal if you are only experimenting.
- Q: Can D.scribe write fiction? A: It is designed for nonfiction from your own recordings. For novels and screenplays, Squibler is the better fit.
- Q: How much does D.scribe cost compared to Squibler's paid tiers? A: D.scribe Starter is $25/month at full price. Squibler Plus is $15.83/month billed annually, normally $29.99/month, and Pro is $49.17/month annually, normally $89.99/month.

### D.scribe vs Dictate

Page: https://www.d-scribe.app/vs/dictate

Dictate sells you a service. D.scribe sells you the tool. One costs about 200 times more and takes far longer, and for some people that is exactly the right trade.

Dictate is not software. It is a done-for-you ghostwriting service that starts around $4,997 and usually begins with a discovery call. It is the most expensive option in the category and, for people who want a human in the loop, the most hands-off.

- What you are buying: D.scribe: Self-serve software you run yourself. Dictate: A service. AI-guided interviews with human involvement and a done-for-you process.
- Price: D.scribe: Starter $25/mo (300 Ink, about 1.5 books), Pro $50/mo (660 Ink, ~3 books, plus about 30 min/month of spoken brainstorming), Premium $100/mo (1,500 Ink, ~7 books, plus about 80 min/month). Dictate: Starts at $4,997 as a one-time project fee. A free discovery call is the entry point.
- Time to first draft: D.scribe: Minutes to hours, because you drive it. Dictate: Weeks, because it is an interview and production process.
- Voice capture: D.scribe: Voice profile built from your uploaded recordings. Dictate: Voice DNA, with a published claim of 95% or higher match.
- How you are guided: D.scribe: Spoken brainstorming on Pro and above. You still make every call. Dictate: Structured AI-guided interviews with a Content Scorecard, plus phone-based sales and onboarding.
- How you test it: D.scribe: 10 Ink free, no call required. Dictate: Discovery call only. You cannot try the product before paying.
- Who does the work: D.scribe: You, with the software doing the drafting. Dictate: Largely handled for you, which is the entire point of the price.

Where Dictate is stronger: Human guidance and a finished result you did not have to drive. If you want to talk to a person, hand over the work, and have someone else manage the process, Dictate is built for that and D.scribe is not.

Pick Dictate if: You have a real budget for your book, you want a guided human process, and you would rather pay for someone else to run it.

Pick D.scribe if: You want to keep control, you want a first draft this week rather than this quarter, and $4,997 is not a number you are willing to spend on a manuscript.

- Q: Is D.scribe a cheaper version of Dictate? A: They are different products. Dictate is a done-for-you ghostwriting service starting around $4,997. D.scribe is software from $25/month that you operate yourself.
- Q: Do I get to talk to a human with D.scribe? A: Not in the way Dictate provides. Spoken brainstorming on Pro and Premium lets the AI interview you out loud, but there is no human ghostwriter or account manager.
- Q: Can I try before paying? A: Yes. D.scribe gives you 10 Ink to start with no call. Dictate's entry point is a free discovery call.
